title: Phosphoproteomic dysregulation promotes tumor proliferation in Cushing's disease.
publicationName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
journalName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
snippet: Pituitary adenomas constitute up to 20% of primary brain tumors, yet somatic mutations are only found in 15% of pituitary adenomas. Epigenomic dysregulation has been proposed as a tumorigenic mechanism in pituitary adenomas causing Cushing's disease (CD).
